notes: 'whom' is read as the fused relative plus resumptive object suffix, the one English word carrying both the relation and the resumption (rules 22, 30); the suffix is 3ms and agrees with the antecedent נָבִיא, so it is genuinely resumptive. The alternative marking the suffix unrepresented is named in that unit's note.
The presentative dummy 'there' of 'there hath not arisen' belongs to the verb's unit; the explicit subject נָבִיא keeps its own English (rule 17).
'like unto' heads on 'like', the lexeme-bearing word rather than the connective (rule 24).
